tips: Version T is the most deliberate and professional open-format transition. Instead of forcing an impossible mix between clashing tempos and keys, it turns Song A's vocal hook into an energetic 16th-note stutter build with a rising high-pass filter, clearing out the low end and dropping Song B cleanly on the one.
Layer a subtle white-noise riser sweep underneath the stutter roll and add a small crash or impact sample on the downbeat of Song B to maximize the drop energy.

Version U executes a textbook professional DJ echo-freeze on the lyrical resolution ('brand new'), allowing the lush reverb tail to decay naturally into the space so Song B's 130 BPM drop lands with full punch, completely eliminating harmonic discord and tempo collisions.
Layer a subtle high-pass filter sweep or white-noise riser on the decaying reverb tail from 21s to 23.5s to build even more anticipation into the drop.
Version T uses a perfectly timed spatial echo and reverb wash on the hook, dissolving the harmonic and tempo clash into an atmospheric transition that lets Song B take over with full driving energy.
Apply a slight high-pass filter sweep to Song A's tail right before the delay freeze to completely clear out low-mid frequencies for Song B's bassline.

Version P lets the full melodic line ('inspire you') breathe and conclude naturally over Song B's rising synth tension, then leaves a clean beat of silence/reverb before dropping the 130 BPM house groove on the one. It avoids both the amateur vocal stutter of Q/T and the sloppy ad-lib clipping heard in R/S/U.
Add a filtered 4-beat drum roll or rhythmic percussion build in the incoming tempo during the final bar to help the dancefloor anticipate the jump from 87 to 130 BPM.
